summary.prose: The build lays down the approval types and the setting first, then the daemon-side broker and its IPC, then the pure policy and the executor change, then the mechanical rewrite of about a hundred builtins behind a before/after snapshot, and last the client prompts and docs. The destructive-always-asks rule is proved at three levels: the pure policy, the executor with a fake broker, and a mode by tool-class matrix through the real executor and broker.

tasks.title: Declare the approval types and the new Tool and ToolDeps fields
tasks.summary: Add ApprovalClass (none, common, destructive), CommonApprovalMode (manual, edit-auto, auto), ApprovalRequest { requestId, toolId, approvalClass, repoPath, arguments, preview, reason, expiresAt }, ApprovalAnswer, ApprovalDenial (declined, timed-out, no-client, cancelled) and ApprovalGate beside the s2 types in src/daemon/tools, plus the optional Tool.approval (a class or a per-input function) and the optional ToolDeps.caller ('agent' | 'daemon' | 'workflow') and approvalMode. requiresApproval and destructive stay for now, so nothing else changes.

ApprovalDenial has exactly declined, timed-out, no-client and cancelled and is assignable to s2's ToolDenialReason
no existing Tool, ToolResult or ToolDeps field changes meaning, and tool ids and input schemas are unchanged

tasks.title: Build the approval broker
tasks.summary: Add the daemon-owned broker (src/daemon/approval-broker.ts): a pending table keyed by requestId with a resolver and a 300 second timer, the set of open approval streams, ask(request) resolving to an answer or an ApprovalDenial (no-client at once with no stream open, timed-out at expiry, declined, cancelled when the caller's signal aborts, which also sends the subscribers a cancel frame), answer(requestId, decision) where the first answer wins and an unknown or already answered id is refused, replay of still-pending requests to a late subscriber, and no-client for every pending request when the last stream closes. It never rejects.
acceptanceChecks: ask() with no open stream resolves no-client without waiting
an unanswered request resolves timed-out at its expiry and a late answer is ignored
two subscribers: the first answer wins and the second is told accepted false
closing the last stream resolves every pending request to no-client
an aborted caller signal resolves cancelled and removes the request
the broker holds no state across a restart and never rejects

tasks.title: Resolve the approval class, the effective mode and the request
tasks.summary: Add the pure resolution used by the executor (src/daemon/tools/approval-policy.ts): the class from the field or the per-input function (a function that throws counts as destructive; absent means none), the rule for whether to ask (destructive always; common when the effective mode, deps.approvalMode else tools.commonApproval, is manual or edit-auto; none never), and the request builder (repository from input cwd then deps.repoPath, the exact arguments truncated for display with the length noted, the preview from buildApprovalGate with a generic preview if it throws, a 300 second expiry). No broker and no IO.

tasks.title: Make executeTool ask before it runs
tasks.summary: In src/daemon/tools/executor.ts run s2's input check, then the approval step from t5: ask the broker for the request, and on a decline, timeout, no client or cancel return a failed result with failure kind denied and the denial reason, without running the tool. Remove the 'auto-approving' branch. Set caller at the two ToolDeps builders that reach executeTool (src/analyze/context/driver.ts, src/agent/providers/ollama.ts). The broker is reached through a daemon-level accessor so executeTool keeps its signature.

tasks.title: Map every builtin onto the approval field
tasks.summary: Rewrite the builtins: requiresApproval true becomes approval 'common', each of the 7 predicates becomes a per-input function returning common or none, requiresApproval false or absent becomes none (the field is dropped), and the 8 destructive: true builtins (cloud az/vm, k8s, aws s3, gcp compute, aws cloudformation, gcp run, gcp storage, aws ec2) become approval 'destructive'. Include src/docgen/tool.ts. Then remove requiresApproval and destructive from the Tool type. A script-assisted, mechanical change that keeps every tool id and input schema; a snapshot of tool id, input schema and old flag taken before the rewrite is kept as a test fixture.
